summary: According to a small computer model rather than human tests, Rifamycin received a high risk score for the liver and a low risk score for the heart [M]. Out of 46 total trials found in a search, one study was stopped because data showed the tested drug combinations could not reach the goal of finding a new three-month tuberculosis treatment [3][5]. Another trial ended early due to slow recruitment and study closure [3][6]. A third trial was stopped because the sponsor changed the drug's development plan, rather than because of safety or effectiveness worries [3][4].
